pattern: a knurl Python writes and the Rust writer cannot
evidence: AP242's turned_knurl WR2 needs six to nine parameters (major and nominal diameter, diametral pitch and three or more of number of teeth, tooth depth, root fillet, helix angle, hand: haecceity pmi/write.rs refuses 'a knurl with 3 parameters (turned_knurl WR2: 6 to 9)', seen on parts/pin); the intent states diameter and pitch only, so no knurl can be written without guessing. Python writes its text route and a UDA. Listed in not_written; questions Q4 and Q15.

pattern: a fit written as its class, read back without stated limits
evidence: A fit is written as the ISO 286 class (LIMITS_AND_FITS, haecceity's Fit) with no stated limits, so the read-back states no deviations; Python writes bare limits because OpenCascade writes the grade wrongly (writer.py docstring: 'SetClassOfTolerance writes the grade wrongly (IT7 is written as grade 9)'). The class determines the same limits by ISO 286 (standards.rs tables); tests/writer.rs the_spool_is_written_verified_and_read_back reads each fit back as its class, g6 and p6 included.

pattern: a g6 diameter Python's reader garbles
evidence: The intent's nominal is 6 (the pin's Ø6 shaft, g6). Python reads back 3.006: OpenCascade's reader cannot return a tolerance whose deviations are both below nominal and garbles the value (writer.py docstring: 'Ø70 g6 reads back as 35.0145'). haecceity reads the nominal as written.

pattern: a g6 diameter Python's reader garbles
evidence: The intent's nominal is 70 (the spool's Ø70 g6, turned_steps:89); Python reads back 35.0145, OpenCascade's garbling of a tolerance wholly below nominal, which writer.py's docstring cites with this very number. haecceity reads 70.

pattern: a distance -0.05/-0.1 Python's reader garbles
evidence: The intent states distance 10, upper -0.05, lower -0.1 (scenario value '-0.05/-0.1'). Python reads back value 5.05 and no deviations: OpenCascade cannot return a tolerance wholly below nominal (writer.py docstring). haecceity reads 10 with -0.05/-0.1, as written.

pattern: a lower deviation Python reads with the wrong sign
evidence: The intent states +0.1/+0.05 (scenario value '+0.1/+0.05', apply: upper 0.1, lower 0.05). Python reads back lower -0.05: OpenCascade's reader loses the lower deviation's sign (writer.py: 'The writer negates the lower tolerance'). haecceity reads +0.05.

pattern: a datum no tolerance references, read back
evidence: Datum A on the plate's top face is in the intent and written; OpenCascade's reader imports a datum only when a tolerance references it (writer.py docstring), which is why the warning exists. haecceity writes and reads it (tests/writer.rs unreferenced_datums_are_warned).

pattern: Python's three parts of one product are one part here
evidence: Python (XCAF) lists CTC-02 as three parts and refuses the assembly for its PMI; haecceity has one part per product definition (question Q7), so Python's three intents name the one Rust part three times and the writer refuses 'a part is written once'. With Q7 settled the comparison applies; an assembly with PMI from elsewhere is written by add mode (Q6).

pattern: Python's two parts of one product are one part here
evidence: As CTC-02: XCAF's two parts are one product definition in haecceity (question Q7); Python's intents name the one Rust part twice.

pattern: Python's parts of one product are one part here
evidence: Python fails inside its text route ('expected one B-rep representation, found 0'); the Rust engine has one part per product definition (question Q7), so Python's per-XCAF-part intents name the one Rust part more than once ('a part is written once').

pattern: Python's parts of one product are one part here
evidence: As CTC-02 RC: Python fails in its text route; Python's per-XCAF-part intents name the one Rust part more than once (question Q7).

pattern: an intent item on no faces, refused where Python fails in OpenCascade
evidence: On 25 mfcadpp parts and cgb217 Python's own intent has a hole's size, locations and position with faces [] (e.g. mfcadpp/1004 holes:16). Python's write then fails inside OpenCascade ('StepShape_DimensionalLocation: Null Reference', or 'expected one B-rep representation, found 0'); the Rust writer refuses the intent as invalid, naming the item ('the size on holes:16 names no faces'), and writes nothing. Question Q17 (write the rest instead?).

pattern: written where Python fails in its text route
evidence: Python fails appending its text route ('expected one B-rep representation, found 0': its anchor search finds no ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION); the intent (material, general tolerance) is written by haecceity and verified by reading back.

pattern: an AP203 file that cannot become AP242, refused with its instances named
evidence: haecceity's decision 1: a file gaining PMI becomes AP242 only if every instance validates against AP242; NIST's AP203 RD/RC files have instances that do not (nist_ctc_01_asme1_rd: '#14 cc_design_approval ... #84 is product_definition, not an entity type of SELECT approved_item'), so the write is refused naming them (WriteError::Refused). Python re-exports the geometry through OpenCascade as AP242DIS, so its file claims a schema its instances need not satisfy.

pattern: an AP203 file that cannot become AP242, refused with its instances named
evidence: The scenario writes corpus nist_ctc_03_asme1_rc, an AP203 file whose instances do not all validate against AP242 (haecceity decision 1); refused naming them, as the corpus case.

pattern: answers stored by Python that Python cannot resume
evidence: Python stores the answers with a fingerprint of the input's faces, then re-exports the geometry through OpenCascade, whose centroids' zero components change sign; its fingerprint of the file it wrote no longer matches (checked: flanged_spool_132, stored f39f4952..., Python's fingerprint of its output c8eb6e8e..., no rounded centroid differs). The Rust writer keeps every geometry byte, so its fingerprint matches and the answers resume.

pattern: a Python-written file does not resume in the Rust engine
evidence: The payload is read (tests/resume.rs pythons_stored_answers_are_read) and its face count matches, but Python's fingerprint hashes OpenCascade's centroids, whose zero components carry other signs than haecceity's (plate: Python [-50.0, -0.0, -0.0], Rust [-50.0, -0.0, 0.0]; equal numbers, tests/resume.rs a_python_fingerprint_differs_only_in_signs_of_zero). The Rust engine cannot verify the faces, so it does not resume (the file is analysed with its PMI as its own). Question Q14.
